findings.reason: §4's done-when is a measurement of behaviour that already has four implementations, so the section should be a measurement plus a localised repair of the recorded host conversion, with the endpoint stated against the existing per-state arrays rather than as new capability.
findings.text: `ForwardProfile.solve_batch` already maps the accelerated routes (`_ACCELERATED = ("picard", "anderson", "newton_krylov")`, `forward.py:196`) over a leading ensemble axis with `jax.vmap`, so the plan's premise that the public solve cannot run under a batch is a premise about one call site, not about the codebase; the same type is implemented at `nova/equilibrium/batched_labeller.py:725` (`jax.vmap(one)` inside a sharded, padded, fixed-shape program whose `BatchedLabelledResult` at `batched_labeller.py:48` already carries `converged`, `termination` and `terminal_residual` as batch-width arrays, read once at `batched_labeller.py:872`), at `nova/equilibrium/support_read.py:2040` (`solve_batch` over booked support, used by `drive_continuation`), and at `nova/equilibrium/profile.py:702` (`solve_batch` for the coefficient-reconstruction path); the plan reads as if batched device solve must be built

findings.reason: the section's seed policy and stop rule should be stated as an application of the existing continuation owner (or a stated reason it cannot carry a coefficient amplitude), because a parallel ladder drifts from the certified warm-start contract — the plan's own §2 negative control depends on that contract being the same one §1's positive control used.
findings.text: `advance_drive` already advances a large drive change in adaptive warm-started sub-steps, seeding each sub-step from the previous converged state (`predict_seed`, `drive_continuation.py:105`), certifying at the target drive against the unchanged fresh residual; §2's ladder of fractions 1/64…1 with "each solve started from the last state that qualified" is that same mechanism driven by a coefficient amplitude instead of a drive, so a bespoke ladder loop would duplicate its acceptance and adaptation logic

findings.reason: a fourth batched surface splits the padding, sharding and host-read rules that §4's agreement clause (1e-9 of the axis-to-boundary span; warm wall per state at width 16 no greater than one unbatched solve) is measured against.
findings.text: the sharding (`batched_labeller.py:727-745`, `NamedSharding` over a device mesh), the batch-width divisibility and padding rule (`batched_labeller.py:766`) and the one-host-read result (`batched_labeller.py:872`) are shared infrastructure already owned by `BatchedLabeller`; §4's "batch of 16 and of 64 copies … one traced program … per-state converged flags and residuals as arrays of the batch width" is exactly that owner's documented contract, so the node must extend `BatchedLabeller` (or route `ForwardProfile.solve_batch` through it) rather than add a third batched call path beside `forward.py:3220` and `support_read.py:2040`

findings.reason: §4 compares batched and unbatched walls and states "the record names that route", which is a receipt property; a batched call that cannot carry the request cannot produce a receipt comparable with the unbatched one.
findings.text: `solve_batch` resolves defaults through the private `_resolve_solve_defaults` and takes `route`/`**options`, while `ForwardProfile.solve` accepts a `ForwardSolveRequest` and returns a `ForwardSolveReceipt` (`forward.py:2823-2888`; the request/receipt types are `nova/equilibrium/solve_request.py:574` and the seam is declared the only supported route in `nova/equilibrium/AGENTS.md`); §4's endpoint therefore needs the seam widened to a batched request/receipt, not a second entry point beside it

findings.reason: the honest change is for the batched path to accept a `ForwardSolveRequest` and return one `ForwardSolveReceipt` per state (or a stacked receipt), which the section should state as its endpoint rather than leaving the batched call outside the seam.
findings.text: the batched entry point forwards to `_solve_accelerated` and adds nothing the seam carries: no receipt, no resolved-defaults block, no `compilation_cache` hit record, so its verdict is not comparable with a production receipt; §4 then needs a wrapper to re-add exactly the fields the seam already defines

findings.reason: the plan does describe the endpoint (stored inputs, per-solve mesh/route/coefficients, terminal reason and residual), and the reuse map belongs to the brief; recorded here so the brief names `nova/imas/equilibrium.py` rather than allowing a second reading path.
findings.text: §1's "stored inputs … each machine's description, imas-efit's fitted conductor currents and profile coefficients, and the stored flux map used as the starting field" is the read `nova.imas.equilibrium.Equilibrium`/`EquilibriumData` (`equilibrium.py:848`) already performs through `Chart`/`GetSlice` (flux map, profiles, grid), with `nova/io/geqdsk.py` for the eqdsk form; the inverse baseline's comparison already reads these three cases (its record is `docs/evidence/fragments/inverse-equilibrium-baseline/efit-comparison.html`), so §1 should name the endpoint as the reproducible receipt of that read, not as a new reader

findings.reason: the plan already binds the correct reporting instrument; this is a brief-level instruction to reuse the painters, not a plan change.
findings.text: §1(3) and §3 ask for a line-contour panel on the stored state with both null sets and the wall, which is the committed painter vocabulary already present (`draw_flux_contours` at `poloidal.py:138`, `contours`, `draw_nulls` at `poloidal.py:540`, `draw_wall` at `poloidal.py:29`, `contour_levels` at `poloidal.py:748`); the plan is correct to require the panels but nothing in it establishes that two fields share one level array except by "shared levels", and `contour_levels` is the mechanism that makes that true

findings.reason: the section must account for the added interface surface in its own text, and naming the merge (one batched entry point replacing the three existing `solve_batch` surfaces, or an explicit statement that no retirement is possible and why) is what turns the section from new capability into the repair its own record describes.
findings.text: with public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0 supplied for this week, §4 ("the public solve runs under a batch") adds a batched form to the public solve's surface — either a batched request/receipt pair or a widened `solve_batch` signature — and its text names nothing it retires or merges and states no reason nothing can be

findings.reason: the plan's endpoint (largest qualifying fraction, smallest non-qualifying fraction, two verdicts, one negative control) is unambiguous and the record shape is the brief's to fix; the deficiency is machinery placement, not endpoint.
findings.text: §2's measure is a ladder plus a two-route comparison against a refusal, and it is stated as per-case narrative with the seed policy restated in prose ("each solve started from the last state that qualified … using its policy"), which is the shallow-surface-per-row shape: three cases, two routes each, a seven-rung ladder, all resolved by hand in the record rather than by one result type that carries (case, route, fraction, qualified, residual, terminal reason)

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — `nova/equilibrium/batched_labeller.py` is already the deep module this endpoint needs (sharding, padding, one host read, fixed-shape record behind three public names), so a design that reaches §4 through `ForwardProfile.solve_batch` plus a new evidence path spreads the same behaviour across shallower surface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the batched device solve has three owners (`forward.py:3220`, `batched_labeller.py:725`, `support_read.py:2040`) and the plan's §4 would add a fourth surface instead of extending one; §1's stored-state read duplicates `nova/imas/equilibrium.py:505`/`:848`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §4 adds a batched form of the public solve (a new request/receipt pair or a new batch entry point) without naming anything it retires or merges, and without stating why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the endpoint of §4 (a batched public forward solve returning per-state converged flags and residuals with no host conversion in the traced solve) is already implemented four times over in this repository (`nova/equilibrium/forward.py:3220`, `nova/equilibrium/batched_labeller.py:476`, `nova/equilibrium/support_read.py:2040`), and §2's warm-started ladder is already owned by `nova/equilibrium/drive_continuation.py:135`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — `ForwardProfile.solve_batch` (`nova/equilibrium/forward.py:3220`) is reachable only with raw solver keywords and cannot accept a `ForwardSolveRequest`, so a node told to "make the public solve run under a batch" would add a batched path beside the seam rather than widen the seam it must not route around.
